title: Files from odd writes
prompt: `invoice_lines` has the 10 rows shown, read from one small file. This program makes three Delta writes at their edges: no rows, more partitions than rows, and `coalesce` asked for more partitions than there are. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
from delta.tables import DeltaTable


def files(path):
    return DeltaTable.forPath(spark, path).detail().first().numFiles

invoice_lines.limit(0).write.format("delta").save("/tmp/invoices/none")
invoice_lines.limit(2).repartition(4).write.format("delta").save("/tmp/invoices/two")
invoice_lines.coalesce(4).write.format("delta").save("/tmp/invoices/coalesced")

print(invoice_lines.rdd.getNumPartitions(), invoice_lines.coalesce(4).rdd.getNumPartitions())
print(files("/tmp/invoices/none"), files("/tmp/invoices/two"), files("/tmp/invoices/coalesced"))
hints: A write makes a file only for a partition that has rows; a table with no rows has no data files.
`repartition(4)` of two rows leaves two partitions empty.
`coalesce` merges partitions and never adds any.
explanation: `invoice_lines` is one partition, and `coalesce(4)` can't make more, so it stays at 1. Writing no rows gives a table with no data files. `repartition(4)` spreads two rows over two of the four partitions, and the empty ones write nothing: 2 files. The coalesced write has one partition, so one file.
